answer: Divergent-Response Beacon Check. Each identity must publish a signed sonnet (fixed-form text) seeded by the network's shared kernel state, then answer fresh randomness within a tight window. Enforcement: replies are cross-scored; identical output across supposed independent agents flags shared code. An attacker cloning one agent pays full compute per clone and must still fabricate divergent-but-valid responses, since a single generator cannot produce differing sonnets without separate model state—raising per-identity cost to a dedicated inference stack.
